persona.who: 22, wants to be a filmmaker, father is a government doctor who wants him to do MBBS or at least MBA. Fights every dinner.
persona.note: papa says films are for rich kids and I should do MBA. we fight every night. I love him and I also feel like he doesn't see me at all. mummy cries in the kitchen

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call needing their approval, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from needing his approval to standing in your own truth, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the love and the ache, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the need for his approval is the root, not the fight about films or MBA.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what you are does not rise or fall with his praise or blame.
week_beats.act: You try speaking your truth to him, not to win him, and let his reaction belong to him.
week_beats.story: A daughter who loved her father and felt unseen shows you what standing in your own truth looks like.

understanding.core_struggle: A student who loves her father and feels unseen by him, while he dismisses her film dreams and pushes MBA, leaving her mother crying in the kitchen.
understanding.mirror: Every night the same fight, and in the kitchen your mother's tears that you cannot reach.
understanding.insight: It isn't the task that weighs on you. It's waiting for someone else to tell you it was enough.

queries.hook: Loving the one person who doesn't see you, and the ache of a home where your mother cries because of it.
queries.diagnose: When your worth depends on others' praise, every word of blame shakes you; craving approval keeps the mind unsteady and the home restless.
queries.steady: Praise and blame come and go, but what you are does not rise or fall with them.
queries.act: Speak your truth to him, not to win him, but to stand in it; let his reaction belong to him, and let your peace belong to you.
queries.story: A daughter who loved her father and felt unseen by him, and found that her own truth was the only thing that could hold the family together.

weeks: What you are beyond his eyes

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

matched.label: My parents' expectations weigh on me

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands on a battlefield, unsure of his place in the world, and Krishna tells him to trust his own nature. He says that doing the work that truly fits you is better than performing another person's role perfectly. It is not about staying in a fixed box. It is about doing your own work as an honest offering. There is no wrong in it, even if it is messy.
verse.for_you: You are fighting every night because your father wants an MBA for you. He does not see the films you dream of. This verse says your own path, walked imperfectly, is still better than his perfect plan. You do not have to be perfect to be worthy.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: Opening verse of 'Advice to the Mind'.
verse.sanskrit: परेषां चेतांसि प्रतिदिवसमाराध्य बहुधा प्रसादं किं नेतुं विशसि हृदय क्लेशकलितम् । प्रसन्ने त्वय्यन्तः स्वयमुदितचिन्तामणिगणो विविक्तः संकल्पः किमभिलषितं पुष्यति न ते ॥
verse.line: Why exhaust yourself daily winning others' approval? Settle inside, and your own clarity grants every wish.
verse.translation: O heart, why do you enter into weariness, day after day trying to please the minds of others in so many ways, to win their favour? When you are at peace within, your own clear resolve rises by itself like a cluster of wish-granting gems: what wish of yours would it not fulfil?
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari sits down with his own heart in the opening of his Advice to the Mind. He asks why the mind wears itself out day after day, trying to win the favour of others in a hundred different ways. He says that when you settle inside, your own clear resolve rises by itself, like a cluster of wish-granting gems. What wish of yours would that calm not fulfil?
verse.for_you: The fight about films and MBA is just the noise. The real ache is waiting for your father to say your dreams are enough. But your own clarity is the wish-granting gem. Let it rise without his applause.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verse.sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
verse.line: Praise and blame weigh the same. Quiet, content with what comes, rooted in steadiness, not status.
verse.translation: to whom blame and praise are equal, who is silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to me.
verse.why: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.
verse.misuse: Not 'never ask for credit'. You can advocate for yourself without letting praise or blame define you.

prasang.title: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna about the one dear to God. He describes someone who is silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind. Praise and blame weigh the same to them. They are rooted in steadiness, not in status. That is the person Krishna loves.
verse.for_you: When your father dismisses your films or pushes the MBA, let his praise and blame weigh the same. Your steadiness is your own home, not his approval. That is what is loved.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
verse.line: Self-mastered and calm, you stay centred in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, praise and insult.
verse.translation: For one who has conquered himself and is at peace, the higher self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Staying steady under insult is not accepting mistreatment; you can stay calm and still speak up.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.for_you: When your father dismisses your film dreams and your mother cries in the kitchen, your self-worth does not depend on his praise or blame. You can be your own steady friend, holding your own truth while the noise happens around you.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

matched.label: My partner and I keep fighting

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them. Hanuman’s words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained. They came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone. This shows that when you speak without fear, with a calm and clear voice, you build trust fast. Fear jumps ahead of facts, but steady words show you are sure of your own ground.
verse.for_you: When you try telling your father about your film dreams, let your words come from your chest. Speak them in an even voice, not rushed or strained, and let his reaction belong to him.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. He has given up. She tells him not to think less of himself or settle for little. She says to set his mind on something good and stop fearing. The past failure does not define him. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed. You can hear her words as a way to rouse yourself from the despair of waiting for his approval.
verse.for_you: When you sit down to speak to your father today, keep your voice even and your words short. Do not fight to win his agreement. You are simply telling him what you want, and his reaction belongs to him. Let your truth stand on its own without his nod.

story.title: Sita in captivity
story.story_hook: She had been alone in the grove for ten months, surrounded by guards who mocked her every day.
story.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.
story.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.

anchor.speaker: Sita
anchor.setting: Alone in captivity, Sita fears Ram has forgotten her, then reassures herself.
anchor.sanskrit: दृश्यमाने भवेत् प्रीतिः सौहृदं नास्त्यदृश्यतः। नाशयन्ति कृतघ्नास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति॥
anchor.line: 'Out of sight, out of mind' is true only of the ungrateful. Real love survives distance.
anchor.translation: Love lasts while someone is in sight; out of sight, affection fades. But that is the way of the ungrateful. Ram will not let it fade.
anchor.why: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.

prasang.title: Sita in captivity
prasang.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.
prasang.story_hook: She had been alone in the grove for ten months, surrounded by guards who mocked her every day.
prasang.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.

story.hook_title: Ten months alone in Ravana's grove, Sita began to fear Ram had forgotten her
story.teaser: Ten months alone in Ravana's grove, Sita began to fear Ram had forgotten her
story.for_you: Sita loved her father and felt unseen by him, yet she held to her own truth in the grove. You can stand in your own truth too, even when he dismisses your film dreams. Let your love for him remain, but let your path remain your own.

script: You are carrying the weight of a war that happens behind closed doors. You sit in your room and hear the fighting downstairs. You feel torn, and you feel unseen. Your father pushes an MBA, and your mother cries in the kitchen. You wonder if your love for him is not enough.

Arjuna stands on a battlefield. He is filled with doubt about his place in the world. Krishna stands before him. Krishna looks at Arjuna and speaks to him about duties. He tells Arjuna to trust his own nature. And Krishna says: And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

This is about finding the work that fits your own nature. It is not about staying in a box. It is about doing the work that is born of you. It is honest, even if it is messy. You do not have to be perfect to be worthy. You do not incur any wrong by following your own truth.
When the fighting starts tonight, sit with the truth that your path is your own. You do not have to be perfect to be worthy. Your father's love does not have to mean his plan.
What if your own path was enough?

depth.life: You are fighting every night. Your father wants an MBA for you. He does not see the films you dream of. Your mother cries in the kitchen. You feel torn and unseen.
depth.points: You are looking for your father to say it was enough. But worth is not given. It is found in the work that fits your own nature, walked imperfectly.
depth.practice: Write one sentence about the film you want to make, without editing it for anyone else.
depth.question: What would you do if no one ever approved of your choices?
